Proposition
[Irreducibility criterion for tetrahedral orbifolds] 1. 13.5.1\group tetrahedra Source: thurston:page-0342

For an orbifold with underlying space $D^3$ and singular locus $\partial D^3$, irreducibility is equivalent to the absence of an essential spherical suborbifold; in the tetrahedral setting every spherical suborbifold bounds a suborbifold ball.
Proof

\sketch Double across the boundary and use the finite spherical classification. An embedded spherical section cuts the doubled tetrahedral model into balls, which descend to the asserted ball-bounding property.

□
